{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2015–16 |team=Indiana Hoosiers |image=Indiana Hoosiers logo.svg |image_size=150 |conference=Big Ten Conference |division= |short_conf= Big Ten |CoachRank= 9 |APRank= 14 |record= 27–8 |conf_record= 15–3 |head_coach=[[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]] |hc_year=8th |asst_coach1=[[Tim Buckley (basketball)|Tim Buckley]] |ac1_year=8th |asst_coach2=[[Chuck Martin (basketball)|Chuck Martin]] |ac2_year=2nd |asst_coach3=[[Rob Judson]] |ac3_year=1st |captain = |stadium=[[Assembly Hall (Bloomington)|Assembly Hall]] |champion= Big Ten Regular Season Champions |bowl=[[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result=Sweet Sixteen }} {{2015–16 Big Ten men's basketball standings}} The '''2015–16 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team''' represented [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]] in the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]], who was in his eighth season with the Hoosiers. The team played its home games at [[Assembly Hall (Bloomington)|Assembly Hall]] in [[Bloomington, Indiana]], as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. This season marked the 40th anniversary of the 32–0 and National Championship [[1975–76 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|1975–76 Hoosiers team]], a feat still unrivaled. To commemorate the anniversary, players' jerseys featured a patch on the back. The Hoosiers also held a public recognition of the undefeated team during halftime of the home game against Wisconsin on January 5, at which the announcement was made that a statue of the seniors and starters would be erected outside the south entrance of Assembly Hall. A new banner was revealed honoring the '76 team as NCAA's #1 All-Time March Madness Team. [[Tom Abernethy]] and [[Bobby Wilkerson]], two players from the team, were inducted into the IU Athletics Hall of Fame.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2015/11/06/indiana-to-honor-undefeated-1976-team-throughout-2015-2016-season/|title=Indiana to honor undefeated 1976 team throughout 2015–2016 season |last=Bozich|first=Alex|work=Inside the Hall|date=November 6, 2015|access-date=November 17, 2015}} IU's season-opener victory against [[2015–16 Eastern Illinois Panthers men's basketball team|Eastern Illinois]] was a milestone game, as it marked 1,000 home wins in Indiana basketball history. IU finished the regular season by winning their 22nd conference title, tying them with in-state rival, [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], for the most conference titles. Indiana finished the season 27–8 overall, 15–3 in the Big Ten to win the Big Ten regular season title outright. They received the #1 seed in the [[2016 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]], where they made an early quarterfinals exit by losing to [[2015–16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]]. The Hoosiers received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Indiana defeated [[2015–16 Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball team|Chattanooga]] and [[2015–16 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen for the third time in five years; however, in the Sweet Sixteen they fell to the [[2015–16 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina Tar Heels]], 101–86. ==Previous season== The [[2014–15 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2014–15 Hoosiers]] went 20–14 overall and 9–9 in the Big Ten Conference (tying for seventh place). Much of the Hoosiers' difficulties were caused by a lack of defense and post presence. The Hoosiers improved over the [[2013–14 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|13–14 season]], in which they did not appear in any postseason tournament, by being selected to play in the NCAA Tournament as a #10 seed in the Midwest region. They made an early exit as the #7 [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]] knocked them off in the second round. Following the season, assistant coach [[Steve McClain]] was hired as the new head coach at the [[UIC Flames men's basketball|University of Illinois-Chicago]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.uicflames.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032315aaa.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2015-09-15 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304191256/http://www.uicflames.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032315aaa.html |url-status=dead }} Tom Crean named [[Rob Judson]], who spent the 2014–15 season as Indiana's director of basketball operations, as McClain's replacement.{{Cite web |url=http://scoop.hoosiershq.com/2015/08/crean-confirms-judson-promotion-staff-addition-iubb/ |title = Crean confirms Judson promotion, staff addition {{!}} Indiana Hoosiers basketball, football, soccer and more: The Hoosier Scoop |access-date=2015-09-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907141725/http://scoop.hoosiershq.com/2015/08/crean-confirms-judson-promotion-staff-addition-iubb/ |archive-date=2015-09-07 |url-status=dead }} ==Preseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" |+ style="{{CollegePrimaryStyle|Indiana Hoosiers|color=white|border=no}}" | Indiana departures |- align=center !
